All 17 tests pass and `go vet` is clean. ## What I did Rewrote `markdown.go` from the original character-by-character scan (with its `pos`/`he`/`listOpened` bookkeeping and index-out-of-range-adjacent loop) into a line-based parser: - **`Render`** — splits the document on `\n` and renders each line in order. State is just two booleans: `inList` (a `
    ` is open) and `listItemOpen` (a `
  • ` is open). A `* ` line opens the list/item or continues it; any other line closes the list first, then renders as a header or paragraph. Any unclosed list/item is closed at the end. - **`renderEmphasis`** — the four `strings.Replace` calls from the original, now isolated with a comment explaining the quirk they preserve: only the first `__` pair and first `_` pair in the whole document are converted. - **`renderLine`** — counts leading `#`s; 1–6 becomes `…`, 7+ falls back to a paragraph (matching the original's h7 behavior). Behavior is preserved for all test cases, including the edge cases: `#######` lines rendered as paragraphs, `#`/`*` inside header/list/paragraph text left literal, and lists closing properly when followed by a plain line (`
      …

    End a list

    `). No test files were modified and no new files were created.
